correctness.rationale: For a strictly positive killed kernel the Perron-conjugated product has the form Q+f(log n)A/n. A positive approximate harmonic vector with normalization n^{-kappa mean(f)} exp[-kappa Psi(log n)] has a componentwise relative O(n^-2) residual. Summation of those residuals constructs an exact harmonic function. The zero-mean Poisson equation and spectral contraction give the uniform O(n^-2) conditioned-kernel remainder. Forward normalized-row contraction yields the survival formula with relative O(n^-1), and periodic-phase subsequences prove the nonregular variation assertion. The two-state Perron and response arithmetic was recomputed exactly; 63 finite assertions passed from the included standalone checker. No finite diagnostic was used to infer an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Time-inhomogeneous perturbations of exactly the inverse-time order can accumulate into survival corrections; a smoothly varying periodic profile in log time is natural in multiscale or aging systems. The theorem pinpoints the phase function, shows loss of ordinary regular variation despite a positive never-killed conditioning limit, and computes the leading state-dependent conditional response in arbitrary finite dimension. The two-state example excludes a mere common-scalar time change. It characterizes a motivated boundary of the recent fixed-coefficient theory.
